questions.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy),\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=0,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}\pi  & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-0=[\begin{aligned}\pi  & 0\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+\pi +0=\pi .
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=y\operatorname{tan}⁡x,\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{tan}⁡x)=\frac{y}{{cos}^{2}⁡x},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{tan}⁡x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{{cos}^{2}⁡x} & \operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=2,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-2=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
2+4+1=7.
$$

questions.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y \\ (x-y)^{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)=2xy,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)={x}^{2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-y)^{2})=2(x-y),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-y)^{2})=-2(x-y)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2xy & {x}^{2} \\ 2(x-y) & -2(x-y)\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}xy+{y}^{2} \\ xy \\ y+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & \bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} \\ y & \bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} \\ \bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy+{y}^{2})=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy+{y}^{2})=x+2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x+2y \\ y & x \\ \frac{1}{x} & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the missing entries are $x+2y,\,$ $x,\,$ and $\frac{1}{x}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}^{2}) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{2}^{2})\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\pi } \\ \sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}0 \\ ∗\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 \\ 0 & ∗\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\pi } \\ \sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}^{2}))=2{x}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}^{2}),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}^{2}))=0 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{2}^{2}))=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{2}^{2}))=-2{x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{2}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}^{2}) & 0 \\ 0 & -2{x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{2}^{2})\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\pi } \\ \sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{\pi } & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{\pi } & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\pi } \\ \sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
-1+(-2\sqrt{\pi })+0=-1-2\sqrt{\pi }.
$$
